key_insight: Sb doping in Na/K-alloyed Cs2BInCl6 double perovskite nanocrystals creates self-trapped excitons whose photoluminescence color and polarization anisotropy are strongly composition-dependent, even though absorption stays nearly unchanged.
engineering_relevance: This work shows how B-site alloying can tune emission fingerprints in lead-free perovskites, offering a route to design optoelectronic materials with controllable color, radiative efficiency, and polarization response.
method: Optical spectroscopy of Sb-doped Cs2BInCl6 nanocrystals across Na-to-K B-site alloying
Ab initio calculations of excitonic states, lattice distortion, and STE formation
Time-resolved polarization anisotropy measurements to test predicted wavefunction structure
evidence_signal: The abstract reports PL tuning from about 2.48 to 2.70 eV while absorption near 3.8 eV remains nearly unchanged, and measured anisotropy closely matches theory.
watch_item: The strong composition dependence appears tied to subtle lattice distortions and STE formation, so device performance may be sensitive to synthesis control and phase/stoichiometry uniformity.
paper_title: Composition-controlled optical fingerprints and anisotropy of self-trapped excitons in double perovskites
